aliases: J/psi suppression at forward rapidity in Pb-Pb collisions at 2.76 TeV

claim.quote: A suppression of the inclusive J/psi yield in Pb-Pb is observed with respect to the one measured in pp collisions scaled by the number of binary nucleon-nucleon collisions.

key_value.note: Nuclear modification factor R_AA for inclusive J/ψ, 0-80% centrality.
key_value.quote: The nuclear modification factor, integrated over the 0-80% most central collisions, is 0.545 +/- 0.032 (stat.) +/- 0.083 (syst.)

name: J/ψ suppression at forward rapidity in Pb-Pb collisions at 2.76 TeV
notes: Classified as a measurement rather than an observation: J/ψ suppression was already established at SPS and RHIC energies before ALICE. This paper measures the effect at LHC energy and reports a suppression factor with quoted uncertainties, so it is not presented as a first observation, even though the abstract says the suppression 'is observed'.

summary.plain: ALICE measured how often J/ψ particles (made of a charm quark and antiquark) survive lead-lead collisions at the LHC. The J/ψ nuclear modification factor is larger than at the SPS and RHIC for the most central collisions, and models that produce J/ψ from charm quarks in a deconfined phase can describe the data.
summary.technical: ALICE measurement of inclusive J/ψ production at forward rapidity (2.5 < y < 4) in Pb-Pb collisions at √sNN = 2.76 TeV: nuclear modification factor R_AA = 0.545 ± 0.032 (stat) ± 0.083 (syst) for the 0-80% most central collisions, with no significant dependence on centrality. The paper states that R_AA is larger than at the SPS and RHIC for most central collisions (the abstract says these features 'appear significantly different from measurements at lower collision energies') and that models including J/ψ production from charm quarks in a deconfined partonic phase can describe the data.

title: J/psi suppression at forward rapidity in Pb-Pb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 2.76 TeV
why_it_matters: Charmonium (J/ψ) production is studied in heavy-ion collisions as a probe of the quark-gluon plasma: in the colour-screening model, the in-medium dissociation probability of quarkonium states is expected to give an estimate of the initial temperature of the system. At LHC energy ALICE finds R_AA larger than at SPS and RHIC for the most central collisions, and reports that models with J/ψ production from charm quarks in a deconfined partonic phase can describe the data.
